incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: Sev2 - Azure francesouth - private peering BGP suppression affecting Dedicated/Private clusters connected via ExpressRoute. Impact: customer traffic blackholed intermittently. Pager at 14:05 UTC.

pagerduty: paging alex_m, oncall-azure - please acknowledge.

alex_m: acked. I'm pulling BGP state and recent telemetry. Assigning triage.

maria_g: I'm on rotation for customer comms. Which clusters are impacted? I see alerts for 3 dedicated pools in eu-west/peer-francesouth.

samir_r: I can see flaps on the vnet-peers and route table updates from the cloud edge. BGP routes to on-prem prefixes are being withdrawn with community 65535:100 which we don't normally see.

oncall-azure: I've opened a support case with Azure NOC, case# AZ-2026-1987. They're seeing suppressed route announcements from the local fabric to our peering. Working with peering team.

alex_m: quick check - redirecting customer traffic via fallback egress cluster in centralus is possible but will add latency. Should we plan failover?

maria_g: For impacted customers on Private, we need to notify that on-prem reachability may be degraded. Samir, what's the risk if we do a failover?

samir_r: Failover plan: update routing policy at edge to prefer backup path (route-map set local-preference 50 -> 100). Quick commands below. Risk: in-flight KV cache misses and higher latency for real-time features.

samir_r: ```
# preview
show bgp neighbors summary | include francesouth
show ip route vrf cust-123 | include 10.40.0.0/16
config router policy set route-map REROUTE-FRANCESHOUTH permit 10
 set local-preference 200
exit
apply route-map REROUTE-FRANCESHOUTH to peering-edge
```

alex_m: I can stage the policy in the canary pool (dedicated-pool-3) first, verify reachability, then roll. Doing it in 2 mins.

oncall-azure: Azure NOC reports a suspected control-plane bug that suppresses certain extended communities when a maintenance job runs on the peering appliance. Working on a hotfix but ETA unknown.

maria_g: I'll draft outbound note to affected accounts: short blurb + mitigation steps + ETA unknown. Keep it calm.

pagerduty: reminder: update incident channel every 15m.

alex_m: canary applied to dedicated-pool-3. Initial checks: on-prem ping restored for 2/3 customers behind that pool. No obvious cache corruption. Running perf tests.

samir_r: Rolling to dedicated-pool-1 now. Command applied. Monitoring BGP table and tcpdump on the peering link.

alex_m: tcpdump shows BGP update withdrawals from our neighbor, then silence. After route-map applied we see our announcements egressing via alternate path.

oncall-azure: Azure pushed a temporary config to force-community-preserve on the fabric, which seems to stop additional suppressions. NOC suggests keeping the workaround until full patch.

maria_g: sent customer note to three affected accounts (private-dedicated customers). Message: "We're experiencing partial on-prem connectivity from Azure francesouth due to a peering control-plane suppression. We've applied a routing workaround that restores reachability via a fallback path; you may see increased latency. We're coordinating with Azure NOC for a permanent fix."

samir_r: monitoring shows stabilized routes for 30m. No new withdraws. Latency delta ~+60ms for failover paths.

alex_m: will keep the route-map in place and mark runbook change. Need postmortem: how this slipped through — our peering health checks didn't catch extended-community suppression.

maria_g: customer success asked if we can automate detection for community changes; logged a request with product.

pagerduty: severity lowered to S3 at 15:10 UTC after stabilization, but keep incident open until Azure provides permanent patch.

oncall-azure: Azure support acknowledged and escalated to engineering. Case updated: hotfix scheduled; they'll notify when patch is rolled.

alex_m: cleanup notes - created follow-up ticket INFRA-6521 for detection rule, INFRA-6522 for runbook update. I'll attach tcpdumps and BGP snapshots.

maria_g: thanks everyone. I'll do a customer follow-up in 2 hours with status. Closing the pager for now. :white_check_mark:
